sections.h2: Where do Nobles County property owners get tax answers?
sections.html:
The Government Center at 315 Tenth Street in Worthington houses both offices you will need. The Auditor-Treasurer answers at 507-295-5258 and takes mail at PO Box 757, Worthington, MN 56187. The Assessor is at 507-295-5208. The Auditor-Treasurer page calls that office the county's property tax administrator and a statutory member of the County Board of Equalization.

The office also handles some items that rarely appear in other counties' summaries: wind energy and transmission line taxes, ditch fund assessments, tax increment financing and mobile home transfers. For a house seller the useful pieces are collecting current and delinquent tax, special assessments and forfeiture proceedings.

The Assessor's page lists forms for homestead, general exemption, blind or disabled homestead and the disabled veteran exclusions. Filing the homestead form is the step that moves a house you live in from the higher nonhomestead class.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Nobles County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Nobles County is in the southwest corner of Minnesota against the Iowa border, on the Buffalo Ridge, where hills reach about 1,995 feet. The county was created in 1857 and organized in 1870, with Worthington platted in 1871 and named seat in 1873. Eleven cities share the map, among them Adrian, Brewster, Ellsworth, Round Lake and Wilmont. Lake Okabena and Lake Ocheda sit in the county, and farming leads the economy, with corn, soybeans and hogs, followed by food processing and metal fabrication.

QuickFacts numbers for the county:

  • 22,338 people in July 2025, only 0.2% above the 2020 base
  • 8,417 housing units, 74.2% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $197,200 and median gross rent of $896
  • 2.80 people per household, and 28.6% of residents under 18
  • 38.3% Hispanic or Latino, with 34.6% of people age 5 and over speaking a language other than English at home
  • Median household income of $66,101 and 94 building permits in 2025

Flat population and a $66,101 income mean buyers here are often local households, so a house priced near $197,200 tends to match what they can finance. Listings and notices in both English and Spanish reach more of that pool.

sections.h2: When do Nobles County property taxes fall due in 2026?
sections.html:
The county's own 2026 calendar splits dates by property type, which is different from the single mid-October date many owners expect:

Nobles County 2026 payment calendar as posted by the Auditor-Treasurer
DateWhat is due
May 15, 2026All taxes, first half
August 31, 2026Mobile home taxes, first half
October 15, 2026City taxes, second half, if applicable
November 16, 2026Farm taxes and mobile home taxes, second half, if applicable

November 15 falls on a Sunday this year, which is why the farm date reads November 16. The second half is not mailed, so keep the first-half stub. The county processes payments within 24 hours of receipt. If you are late, call the office at 507-295-5258 to learn the penalty to include, since the state sets it under section 279.01: 2% on homestead and 4% on other property for the first missed date, rising monthly to caps of 8% and 12%.

sections.h2: What are the ways to pay in Nobles County?
sections.html:
The county lists six methods on its property tax page:

  • Mail a check payable to Nobles County Auditor-Treasurer with the stub from every parcel; the postmark must be on or before the due date
  • Direct payment plan, which pulls the amount from a checking or savings account until you cancel
  • Online by card or e-check, with convenience fees
  • In person at the Government Center by check, cash or card
  • The drop box outside the main entrance on the 10th Street side, open around the clock
  • Escrow through a mortgage lender, which applies when the lender's name appears at the top of the statement

The county will not take post-dated checks, and a private postage meter mark does not prove timely mailing. The office also reminds owners that liability for the tax stands even if a statement never arrives.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Nobles County valuation?
sections.html:
Only the estimated market value for the current assessment year can be contested, according to the Board of Appeal and Equalization handbook posted by the county, and the number is struck as of January 2. Rather than the tax amount, the board reviews the value and class behind it. Call the Assessor first to check the facts on your notice.

  1. Go to your local board, or the open book session if your area holds one. Valuation notices must be mailed at least 10 days beforehand.
  2. If the result still looks wrong, take it to the County Board of Equalization. In 2026 it met on June 16 at 6:00 PM, and the board may sit up to 10 consecutive meeting days in June after the second Friday.
  3. File with the Minnesota Tax Court or district court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, per section 278.01.

Neither board can grant special program status, such as Green Acres. Those need their own application, and a board may not give relief to an owner who refused the assessor entry to inspect.

sections.h2: What should a Nobles County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for any balance on the parcel, since delinquent tax and unpaid special assessments surface at transfer. Under section 272.12, the auditor looks up delinquent tax when a deed arrives, and the recorder refuses a deed lacking the "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" stamp.

The same page lists tax forfeiture proceedings among the office's duties, and the county advertises forfeited land for public sale. Selling well ahead of that stage keeps the choice with you. Confirm whether your lender collects through escrow, because an escrow refund and a seller's own prepaid half can overlap near closing. Ask for both figures in writing.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for Nobles County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call 507-295-5258 for the Auditor-Treasurer, who collects tax. The Assessor, who sets value and class, is at 507-295-5208. Both are in the Government Center at 315 Tenth Street, Worthington.

faqs.q: Why is the farm tax date November 16 in 2026?
faqs.a: The usual agricultural date of November 15 lands on a Sunday this year. Nobles County posts November 16, 2026 for farm and mobile home second-half payments, so the deadline moves to Monday.

faqs.q: Does Nobles County mail second-half tax statements?
faqs.a: No. The county does not mail second-half statements, so you must keep the stub from the first mailing. Taxpayers remain responsible for payment even when no statement reaches them.

faqs.q: Can I use the drop box for a late-night payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The drop box outside the Government Center's main entrance on 10th Street is accessible 24 hours a day. A mailed payment instead needs a postmark on or before the due date.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Nobles County tax bill amount?
faqs.a: You can contest the estimated market value or classification, not the tax amount itself. Start with the Assessor, then the local board or open book, then the County Board, and file any Tax Court petition by April 30.
